title: See where a question lands among the chunks
goal: Make 'similar meaning, nearby vectors' visible, and find out how much a 2D picture can be trusted.
question: What is SPI slave underrun?
look_for: Do the chunks of one module sit together, apart from the other modules?
How much of the variation do the two axes keep? Everything else is not on the screen.
In the table, compare each neighbour's true rank with its rank on the map. Where they differ, the picture is misleading at that spot.

title: Small chunks against large chunks
goal: See what chunk size does to the number, evenness and overlap of chunks before paying for a re-ingest.
look_for: How many chunks does each side make, and how uneven are they (smallest against largest)?
How many characters are stored twice because of overlap on each side?
Open a small chunk on side B. Does it still make sense on its own, or did it lose the sentence that says what it is about?

title: Paragraph chunking against heading chunking
goal: See why structure-aware chunking suits documents with numbered sections.
look_for: On side B every chunk should start at a section heading. Does one section ever get split?
Look at the Section column on side A: where does a chunk start in the middle of a section?
Which side would you rather retrieve for a question about one register?

title: Retrieve 3 chunks or 8
goal: Watch recall and noise trade against each other as top_k grows.
question: What is bit timing?
look_for: Which chunks does only side B have? Are they evidence, or distractors from another topic?
Does the top result change? More results is not better ranking.
Every extra chunk is prompt text the model must read on every question.

title: Check an answer against its sources
goal: Read an answer the way a reviewer would: every claim traced to a numbered passage.
question: What happens if NBRP and DBRP are different?
look_for: Does the answer put a [n] after its statements? Open each cited passage and check it says that.
Which retrieved passages were never cited? Were they needed?
Is there a citation number that matches no passage? The check under the answer says so.

title: Measure instead of looking
goal: Get numbers for the dense baseline and one change, on a fixed set of questions.
look_for: Recall, MRR and nDCG for both presets. Which moved, and by how much?
Open the per-question results: which question changed? Can you explain why from its wording?
A change you cannot trace to specific questions is a coincidence waiting to reverse.

title: Hybrid search rescues an exact identifier
goal: See keyword search find a rare token that the embedding of a whole question smears away.
question: What is published in qualification report QR-4471-B?
look_for: Is the chunk that contains QR-4471-B in side A's results at all?
In pipeline B, read 'BM25 keyword search' and then 'Reciprocal rank fusion': the 'found by' column shows which list contributed each chunk.
The scores change units between the sides: a distance on A, an RRF score on B.

title: MMR trades relevance for variety
goal: Watch near-duplicate chunks get replaced by different ones.
question: What is bit timing?
look_for: Which chunks did MMR drop, and were they saying the same thing as one it kept?
Did a chunk from a different file come in?
Did the best chunk keep its place? Diversity can demote the strongest evidence.

title: Read a little before and after each hit
goal: See neighbor expansion widen the context without changing what was found.
question: How does bus-off recovery work?
look_for: The two sides list the same chunks: neighbor expansion changes the text handed to the model, not the ranking.
In pipeline B, 'Neighbor expansion' shows each chunk's size before and after.
This is why a source-file metric cannot measure this technique: nothing about which files were found changed.

title: A question whose answer is in two places
goal: Find out whether your chat model can notice what is missing and search for it.
question: What does the errata triggered by an NBRP/DBRP time-quantum mismatch cost in throughput?
look_for: In pipeline B, the 'Multi-hop follow-up' stages show the follow-up queries the model wrote, or why the loop stopped.
Did a follow-up name the errata (CHEN0)? If it only rephrased the question, the planner is the weak part, not the search.
Each hop cost one chat call. Was a new chunk found for it?

title: Let the model choose its own searches
goal: Watch an agent split a two-part question, and see what each step costs.
question: Compare the CAN error code ERR080082 with the SPI report QR-4471-B
look_for: Read the agent's steps above the answer. Did it search once per part of the question?
Did it stop by itself, or run to the step budget? 'Evidence gathered by the agent' says why it ended.
Ask the same question again. Did it take the same steps? A fixed pipeline would.
